body:
# Independent audit of the sharp energy–retained-volume comparison


sections of
`candidate da4697fe92a737cb`
after independently deriving the proof below. Reran
`supporting computation verify_energy_retained_total_volume_and_mixing_obstruction_defect_transport.py`:
**1,094 exact checks PASS**. The source's parameter eta=(T/V)^(1/d)
is the reciprocal of r used in this audit; its c is -b below.

The independently derived statement is

    E_K(y) <= (d+1)T_K(y)
                 -d T_K(y)^(1+1/d) |K|^(-1/d),        (1)

for a full-dimensional compact convex K in R^d, d>=1, and y in its
interior. Here T is the largest mass of a density 0<=f<=1_K having
barycenter y, and E is the ordinary projective volume energy. The
analytic proof below passes independently and agrees with the final
written source, including its equality and dimension-one qualifications.

This audit checks the sharp constant, actual retained cap, support
endpoints, both section comparisons, and cone equality. It does not
invoke an unproved mixed-measure depth statement.

## 1. The retained mass really is one actual centroidal cap

Translate y to zero. The hinge functional

    G(u)=integral_K (1+u.x)_+ dx

is continuous and coercive: the own interior ball gives a lower bound
c|u|. It therefore attains a minimum. Its derivative is
integral_(K intersect {1+u.x>=0}) x dx; the exceptional hyperplane has
zero d-volume for u!=0, and near u=0 the hinge is everywhere positive.
Dominated differentiation is justified on the compact body. Thus the
minimizer's actual cap D has centroid zero, and

    G(u_*)=|D|.

For any dominated density with zero first moment,
integral f=integral (1+u_*.x) f<=G(u_*). The indicator of D attains
this bound. This proves existence and exact identification of T.
It is the already audited hinge argument in
`candidate 49e262af8d182671`.

If T=V, the entire body has centroid zero; E=T=V and (1) is equality.
Conversely a centroid at zero gives that case. Henceforth T<V. Then
u_*!=0 and D is a proper cap. Write t=u_*.x, so

    D=K intersect {t>=-1},
    integral_D t dx=0.

The cutting plane meets the interior. Its coarea density f(t) is
section area divided by |u_*|, NOT just unnormalized Euclidean area.
This constant normalization is retained throughout.

## 2. The top endpoint and the retained convex-order comparison

Write the actual projection interval as [alpha,B]. Since the retained
cap is proper and contains the marked point in its interior,
alpha<-1<0<B. For d>=2, f^(1/(d-1)) is concave on (alpha,B).

Choose any actual top point at height B. Homotheties of D toward it
give retained survival mass at least
T[(B-t)/(B+1)]^d for -1<=t<=B. Integrating the survival function of
t+1 gives

    1=mean_D(t+1)>=(B+1)/(d+1),

so B<=d. This uses actual homothetic subbodies, not a presumed cone.

Set

    g_infinity(t)=c(d-t)^(d-1),  t<=d,
    c=dT/(d+1)^d.

Its restriction to [-1,d] has the SAME mass T and first moment zero
as the actual retained law. Extend f by zero outside its support.
The difference of section roots

    f(t)^(1/(d-1))-c^(1/(d-1))(d-t)

is concave on the actual support. On [-1,d] its positive set is an
interval, since B<=d and beyond B the density difference is negative.
If the densities differ, matching mass and first moment force this
positive interval to lie strictly inside (-1,d): a positive-then-
negative difference alone would have a strictly negative first moment
after subtracting its crossing point times its zero mass; the reversed
case is similarly impossible. Thus the signs are -,+,-, with zeros
allowed. The section-root comparison at -1 is nonpositive.

Subtracting the secant line of any finite convex kernel through the
two crossings gives

    integral_(-1)^d w(t) f(t) dt
       <= integral_(-1)^d w(t) g_infinity(t) dt          (2)

for convex w. For a strictly convex w, inequality is strict unless the
retained densities agree almost everywhere. If they agree, their roots
agree throughout the open retained interval by continuity.

Concavity also gives

                  f(t)<=g_infinity(t), t<-1.            (3)

In the nonidentical case, a positive root difference at some s>-1,
together with its nonpositive value at -1, forces a negative difference
at each actual t<-1 by the concavity inequality across -1. In the
identical case, comparison with any retained interior point gives the
weak inequality. Outside the actual support f=0. All endpoint values
are immaterial to these integrals; no atom is present in a linear
projection of a full-dimensional uniform convex-body measure.

## 3. The exterior comparison retains the missing volume exactly

Put

    r=(V/T)^(1/d)>1,
    a=d-(d+1)r<-1,
    g(t)=g_infinity(t) 1_[a,d](t).

Then integral g=V, and its retained restriction still has mass T and
first moment zero. Its exterior mass on [a,-1] equals V-T, the actual
exterior mass. By (3), the exterior difference f-g is nonnegative
below a and nonpositive on (a,-1). Therefore for ANY increasing kernel
w for which these integrals exist,

    integral_(-infinity)^(-1) w f
       <= integral_a^(-1) w g.                         (4)

Indeed subtract w(a); the integrand (w-w(a))(f-g) is nonpositive on
both sides, and the subtracted constant integrates to zero. This is
the exact stochastic ordering needed for the sharp refinement. It
does not require the actual lower endpoint to be at least a; the
actual body may extend farther left.

For strictly increasing w, equality in (4) forces f=g almost
everywhere on the exterior half-line. The matched mass argument does
not replace exterior volume by an infinite cone or discard it.

## 4. Admissible optimizing parameter and exact constant

Let D_0=(d+1)r-d>1 and choose

    b=(r-1)/D_0>0,
    w(t)=(1-bt)^(-d-1).

Because B<=d,

    1-bt>=1-bd=r/D_0>0

on the entire actual body. Thus the parameter -b u_* is admissible in
the full projective energy problem. The kernel is increasing and
strictly convex, so (2) and (4) apply on their respective pieces.

At the comparison cone endpoints,

    L_top=1-bd=r/D_0,
    L_base=1-ba=r.

The exact cone integral is

    integral_a^d c(d-t)^(d-1)(1-bt)^(-d-1)dt
       =V/[L_top L_base^d]
       =T[(d+1)-d/r].                                 (5)

For direct verification, set s=d-t and H=d-a. The antiderivative of
s^(d-1)/(L_top+bs)^(d+1) is
s^d/[d L_top(L_top+bs)^d]. Since cH^d/d=V, (5) follows.
Equivalently this b maximizes (1-bd)(1-ba)^d; its logarithmic
derivative vanishes exactly at b=(a+1)/[(d+1)a].

Consequently

    E <= integral f w <= integral g w
       =(d+1)T-d T^(1+1/d)V^(-1/d),

which proves (1). No minimum/limit interchange is used: one explicit
parameter is tested in the actual body, and two actual density
comparisons bound its value.

## 5. Equality is geometrically a cone, not just a density assertion

When d>=2 and T<V, the kernel above is strictly convex on the retained
range and strictly increasing on the exterior. Equality in (1) forces
both comparisons to be equalities, so the FULL actual section density
equals g on [a,d], and is zero outside, almost everywhere. Its root is
continuous on the open projection interval, so it has the exact affine
profile there. In particular the actual projection endpoints are a,d.

As t decreases to a, sections converge in Hausdorff distance to the
endpoint section: upper inclusion is compactness; lower approximation
comes from interpolating each endpoint point with one fixed interior
point. Thus the base section has positive (d-1)-volume equal to the
limit of the prescribed density (times the coarea normal factor).
Choose any top point at t=d. Its cone over the base section lies in K
and has the SAME section volume at every interior level. Included
compact convex sections of equal positive volume coincide. Closure
therefore identifies K with that actual cone and forces its top face
to be a singleton. This proof also excludes a hidden larger top face
or an exceptional zero-volume appendage of the full-dimensional body.

The marked point lies on the segment joining the apex to the base
centroid, because the actual retained top cap has centroid y. More
precisely its distance fraction from the apex toward the base centroid
is d/[(d+1)r], no greater than the centroid fraction d/(d+1).

Conversely any cone over a full convex (d-1)-base, with such an axial
mark on the apex side of its centroid, attains (1). The displayed top
cap has centroid y, so the hinge certificate proves its maximality T.
After a volume-preserving shear aligning the axis, all parallel
section centroids lie on that axis. The optimizer in (5) has zero
weighted vertical first moment; the horizontal ones vanish as well.
Thus it is stationary for the full energy, hence optimal by strict
parameter convexity. No symmetry of the base shape is required.

All fractions T/V in (0,1) occur in these marked cones. At T=V every
centroidal body attains (1), so the cone classification is not imposed
there.

For d=1, K=[-l,r] about y=0 has T=2m with m=min(l,r), V=l+r, and
E=4lr/(l+r). Then

    2T-T^2/V=4m(V-m)/V=E.

Thus every interval/mark attains (1); no invalid section-root argument
is used in dimension one.

## 6. Exact consequence for the inverse energy-depth certificate

Use the already proved containing-cap function

    F_d(alpha)=((d+1)^(d+1)/d^d) alpha(1-alpha^(1/d)),
    0<=alpha<=Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

It is continuous and strictly increasing on this interval, mapping it
onto [0,1]. For tau=T/V,

    F_d(Gamma_d tau)=(d+1)tau-d tau^(1+1/d).            (6)

Combining (1) and (6) and applying the increasing inverse gives

    V F_d^(-1)(E/V) <= Gamma_d T.                     (7)

Thus the sharp inverse-energy ordinary cap guarantee never exceeds
the elementary ordinary-Grunbaum guarantee obtained from the actual
centroidal retained cap. The assertion compares these certificates;
it does not identify the actual smallest cap volume with either one.
For noncentroid d>=2 marks, equality in (7) is exactly the marked cone
case above; for d=1 it is always equality. At any centroid both sides
are Gamma_d V.

This does not erase the different joint-concavity or whole-body
equality information carried by E. It does rule out an improvement
of the ordinary pointwise cap certificate from E alone over the known
physical retained mass T at that same point.

The source also cites the separately proved joint Minkowski concavity
of T. That stronger dependence is not needed for (1) or the pointwise
certificate comparison (7), and this audit does not silently re-audit
its equality or deepest-stratum consequences. The geometric conclusion
checked here is exactly the ordinary sharp E--T--V theorem and its
stated scalar consequence.
